problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating a Vector Projection Using Components
examples.problem: Let $\mathbf{a}=\langle 1,-3,5 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 5,-4,0 \rangle$. Find the vector projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}$.
examples.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 5+(-3)\cdot (-4)+5\cdot 0}{{5}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{17}{41}⟨5,-4,0⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{85}{41},-\frac{68}{41},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Suppose that $|\,p\,|=4\sqrt{2}$, $|\,q\,|=16$ and that the angle between the vectors is $\theta ={45}^{∘}.$ Find the vector projection of $q$ onto $p$ in terms of the vector $p.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the scalar projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{p}\,q & =|\,q\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =16\operatorname{cos}⁡({45}^{∘}) \\  & =16\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =8\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the unit vector that is parallel to $p:$

$$
u=\frac{p}{|\,p\,|}=\frac{p}{4\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}p
$$

Finally, we compute the vector projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{p}\,q & ={\text{comp}}_{p}\,q\cdot u \\  & =8\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}p \\  & =2p\end{aligned}
$$
